name: Zero Trust
mantra: Never trust, always verify every request.
when_to_apply: Designing network access policies for cloud workloads
Protecting mission-critical workloads from lateral movement
Implementing identity-based access across application layers
Responding to an assumed-breach security posture
Segmenting workloads in multi-tenant environments
without_it: Lateral movement after a single breach compromises entire network
Implicit trust allows unauthorized access between services
Overly permissive network policies go undetected
Insider threats exploit flat network topologies
Compliance failures due to lack of access verification
key_tradeoff: Stronger security verification increases complexity and may add latency versus the risk of implicit trust.

name: Reliability Design Principles
mantra: Design every workload to survive failure and keep serving its purpose.
when_to_apply: Starting architecture design for a new workload
Reviewing existing systems for reliability gaps
Defining SLAs and recovery objectives with stakeholders
Making tradeoff decisions between cost and uptime
without_it: Cascading failures from unplanned outages
No clear recovery strategy when things break
Misaligned reliability targets with business needs
Reactive firefighting instead of proactive resilience
Inconsistent reliability practices across teams
key_tradeoff: Higher reliability demands more redundancy and complexity, increasing cost and operational overhead.

name: Assume Breach
mantra: Design every defense as if the attacker is already inside.
when_to_apply: Designing network segmentation and containment strategies
Planning encryption for data at rest and in transit
Building incident response and disaster recovery plans
Evaluating whether primary security controls have compensating backups
Architecting zero trust access policies
without_it: Single perimeter failure leads to total compromise
Sensitive data exfiltrated due to lack of encryption inside the network
No containment limits blast radius of an attack
Missing audit trails make breach detection impossible
Recovery plans never tested against realistic compromise scenarios
key_tradeoff: Increased operational complexity and cost of layered defenses versus the risk of catastrophic loss from a single point of failure.

name: Four Vs Of Big Data
mantra: Know your data's volume, velocity, variety, and veracity before architecting anything.
when_to_apply: Designing a new big data platform on Azure
Evaluating data pipeline architecture requirements
Choosing between storage and processing technologies
Assessing data quality and governance needs
without_it: Under-provisioned storage or compute that cannot handle data volume
Pipelines that fail under real-time ingestion demands
Brittle systems that break when data formats change
Decisions made on untrustworthy or unvalidated data
key_tradeoff: Optimizing for all four Vs simultaneously increases cost and complexity, so you must prioritize based on workload needs.

name: Design For Recovery
mantra: Assume failure will happen and engineer your way back from it.
when_to_apply: Architecting new workloads that require high availability
Defining RTO and RPO targets for critical systems
Deploying stateful services where data loss is unacceptable
Planning for regional or zonal outages
without_it: Extended downtime with no clear path to restoration
Permanent data loss from unrecoverable failures
Cascading failures spreading across dependent systems
Panic-driven recovery efforts that worsen the incident
key_tradeoff: Recovery capabilities add cost and complexity that must be balanced against the business impact of downtime.

name: Least Privilege
mantra: Grant only needed access, scope, and time
when_to_apply: Assigning RBAC roles to users, managed identities, or pipelines
Configuring Entra PIM for production control plane access
Designing API authorization scopes or Key Vault access policies
Onboarding workloads, team members, or CD pipelines
Auditing existing permissions for privilege drift
without_it: Compromised managed identity escalates across entire subscription
Malicious admin deletes Key Vault secrets via standing access
Accidental broad RBAC assignment exposes production data plane
Audit failure: overprivileged accounts violate SE:05 compliance requirements
Incident response stalls—cannot isolate blast radius from shared privileges
key_tradeoff: Tighter RBAC and PIM activation reduce blast radius but add latency, pipeline friction, and Entra ID as a critical dependency.

name: Zero-Downtime Deployment
mantra: Ship fearlessly without ever turning off the lights.
when_to_apply: Releasing new versions of mission-critical workloads
Applying infrastructure changes to production scale units
Rolling out hotfixes under active user traffic
Migrating backend services with strict SLA requirements
without_it: Planned maintenance windows that erode availability targets
Failed deployments causing full service outages
Customer-visible errors during release rollouts
Fear-driven release culture with infrequent, risky big-bang deploys
key_tradeoff: Achieving zero downtime demands additional infrastructure complexity and cost (e.g., blue-green or canary patterns) in exchange for uninterrupted availability.

name: Design For Resilience
mantra: Build systems that bend but never break.
when_to_apply: Architecting distributed systems with multiple failure domains
Defining SLAs and availability targets for critical workloads
Identifying and hardening the critical path of a workflow
Planning for partial outages or dependency failures
without_it: Total system outage from a single component failure
Cascading failures across dependent services
Users experience hard errors instead of reduced functionality
No clear understanding of which failures matter most
key_tradeoff: Increased architectural complexity and cost versus the degree of resilience gained under failure conditions.

name: Verify Explicitly
mantra: Never trust, always validate every identity, action, and location.
when_to_apply: Authenticating users or services accessing resources
Processing data change requests from any source
Granting access across network boundaries
Evaluating requests from unexpected locations or devices
without_it: Implicit trust allows lateral movement by attackers
Compromised credentials go undetected
Unauthorized data modifications corrupt integrity
Over-privileged access increases blast radius of breaches
key_tradeoff: Stronger explicit verification increases security but adds latency and friction to user and service interactions.

name: Microsoft Zero Trust Model
mantra: Never trust, always verify every request.
when_to_apply: Designing IAM with Entra ID, PIM, RBAC, or Managed Identities
Micro-segmenting networks via NSGs, Private Link, micro-perimeters
Enforcing governance with Azure Policy on control plane
Migrating on-prem workloads—eliminating implicit trust assumptions
Running security design reviews (SE:01–SE:12) or threat models
without_it: Lateral movement after single compromise across flat networks
Standing admin access enables malicious-admin escalation attacks
Credentials in code leak via compromised service principals
No Azure Policy: authorized users bypass security configurations unchecked
Breaches undetected—no assume-breach compensating controls in place
key_tradeoff: Reduced blast radius and explicit verification vs. added latency (identity network traversal), complexity (Entra ID as critical dependency), and misconfiguration risk.

name: Cost-Efficiency Mindset
mantra: Spend only what you must to maximize every dollar's return.
when_to_apply: Starting a new cloud workload design
Reviewing monthly cloud spend reports
Provisioning SDLC and non-production environments
Evaluating whether to scale up or optimize existing resources
without_it: Unchecked resource sprawl and overprovisioning
No accountability for cloud spending decisions
Non-production environments running at production scale
Reactive cost management instead of proactive governance
key_tradeoff: Minimizing cost aggressively can compromise performance, reliability, or delivery speed if taken too far.

name: Design For Rate Optimization
mantra: Squeeze more value from every committed dollar.
when_to_apply: Reviewing resource spend without changing architecture
Choosing consumption-based vs fixed-price billing models
Negotiating Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, or enterprise agreements
Applying Azure Hybrid Benefit or preproduction subscription pricing
without_it: Pay-as-you-go defaults waste 30-60% vs Reserved Instance pricing
Unused Azure Hybrid Benefit entitlements leave license value stranded
Log Analytics stays on per-GB tier despite predictable ingest volumes
Single-tenant deployments miss density savings from co-location
key_tradeoff: Commitment-based discount depth versus consumption-based flexibility and zero-waste billing.

name: Defense-In-Depth
mantra: Never rely on a single layer of security—stack your defenses.
when_to_apply: Designing network segmentation and boundary controls
Implementing compensating controls for identified threats
Architecting multi-tier applications with sensitive data
Applying Zero Trust principles across workload components
without_it: Single point of compromise leads to full breach
Lateral movement goes undetected across flat networks
One misconfigured control exposes the entire system
Threat actors bypass the sole security boundary trivially
key_tradeoff: Each additional security layer adds complexity and potential latency versus the risk reduction it provides.

name: Blast Radius
mantra: Contain every failure before it contains you.
when_to_apply: Designing fault isolation boundaries between components
Evaluating multi-tenant density and co-location risks
Planning deployment stages and progressive rollouts
Assessing impact of a single component failure on dependent flows
without_it: A single fault cascades across the entire workload
Tenant noisy-neighbor problems cause widespread outages
Security compromises spread unchecked through co-located resources
No clear understanding of failure impact during incident response
key_tradeoff: Smaller blast radius requires more isolation boundaries, increasing cost and operational complexity.

name: Automation
mantra: Automate everything you'd regret doing by hand twice.
when_to_apply: Deploying infrastructure or application changes
Running repetitive operational tasks
Scaling workloads to meet demand
Executing test suites across environments
Responding to monitoring alerts with remediation
without_it: Human errors in deployments cause outages
Inconsistent environments lead to drift and bugs
Slow response to incidents due to manual steps
Technical debt accumulates from unscripted processes
Teams cannot scale operations beyond a few workloads
key_tradeoff: Upfront investment in building and maintaining automation versus the ongoing cost and risk of manual processes.

name: Cost-Management Discipline
mantra: Make every dollar visible, owned, and intentional.
when_to_apply: Standing up a new cloud workload or environment
Monthly or quarterly budget review cycles
When cloud spend trends upward unexpectedly
Onboarding new teams to shared infrastructure
without_it: Uncontrolled cloud sprawl and bill shock
No one owns or explains cost overruns
Optimization efforts are reactive and ad-hoc
SLA investments can't be justified against their cost
key_tradeoff: Rigorous cost tracking adds process overhead that must be balanced against team agility and speed of delivery.

name: Design For Usage Optimization
mantra: Squeeze every drop of value from every resource you provision.
when_to_apply: Workload costs are growing faster than business value
Resources sit idle during off-peak periods
Scaling patterns are predictable enough to pre-commit
Multiple regions or instances serve redundant traffic
without_it: Chronic overprovisioning and wasted spend
Idle resources consuming budget with no return
Missed discount opportunities on predictable workloads
Inability to meet SLAs despite high spending
key_tradeoff: Maximizing utilization increases efficiency but reduces headroom for unexpected demand spikes.

name: CAP Theorem
mantra: Pick two: consistency, availability, or partition tolerance—you cannot have all three.
when_to_apply: Designing distributed databases with multiple replicas
Choosing between strong and eventual consistency models
Architecting globally distributed applications
Evaluating database technologies for resilience requirements
without_it: Assuming a distributed system can be perfectly consistent and always available
Unexpected data staleness surprising users and downstream systems
Over-engineering for consistency at the cost of availability
Choosing databases that don't match actual workload trade-off needs
key_tradeoff: Consistency versus availability during network partitions, forcing architects to prioritize one over the other.

name: Self-Preservation
mantra: Design every component to protect itself so failures stay local.
when_to_apply: Designing service boundaries and modular components
Implementing retry, circuit-breaker, or bulkhead patterns
Evaluating cascading failure risks in distributed systems
Planning for partial outages or dependency degradation
without_it: Single component failure cascades across the entire workload
Downstream services overwhelmed by upstream retries
Total outage from a localized incident
No graceful degradation under stress
key_tradeoff: Stronger isolation and self-preservation patterns add complexity and latency versus simpler but more fragile designs.

name: Design For Operations
mantra: Anticipate failure before your customers discover it.
when_to_apply: Architecting a new production workload
Defining testing and deployment pipelines
Establishing monitoring and alerting strategies
Preparing for incident response readiness
without_it: Failures surface only in production via customer complaints
No telemetry to diagnose issues under pressure
Slow and chaotic incident response
Recurring outages with unknown root causes
Operational toil dominates engineering capacity
key_tradeoff: Investing upfront in observability and failure testing increases initial effort but dramatically reduces mean time to recovery.

name: Observable Systems
mantra: If you can't see it, you can't fix it.
when_to_apply: Designing distributed microservices architectures
Setting up production monitoring and alerting
Troubleshooting intermittent failures across services
Onboarding SRE teams to a new system
Establishing health models for critical workloads
without_it: Blind spots in production lead to prolonged outages
Teams resort to guesswork during incident response
Correlated failures go undetected until customer impact
No holistic view of system health across components
Mean time to recovery increases dramatically
key_tradeoff: More telemetry improves visibility but increases cost, complexity, and potential performance overhead.

name: Simplicity
mantra: Reduce the surface area before you try to control it.
when_to_apply: Designing a new architecture from scratch
Reviewing systems with frequent misconfigurations
Consolidating redundant components or services
Onboarding new teams to an existing platform
Choosing between competing design approaches
without_it: Sprawling configurations that no one fully understands
Increased misconfiguration and outage risk
Slower incident response due to hidden complexity
Higher onboarding cost for new engineers
Drift from standards as teams create workarounds
key_tradeoff: Simplicity may limit flexibility and feature richness, requiring discipline to resist over-engineering.

name: Segmentation
mantra: Draw boundaries before attackers draw their own.
when_to_apply: Designing network topology for a new workload
Defining team access boundaries and responsibilities
Isolating sensitive data stores from general compute
Planning multi-tenant or multi-environment architectures
Containing blast radius after a security incident
without_it: Lateral movement across the entire environment after a single breach
Overly broad access permissions for users and services
Inability to apply distinct security policies per workload tier
Compliance failures due to lack of data isolation
Blast radius of failures or attacks spans the whole system
key_tradeoff: Finer-grained isolation increases security posture but raises complexity and total cost of ownership.

name: PACELC Theorem
mantra: Even when things are fine, you're still trading latency for consistency.
when_to_apply: Choosing between eventual and strong consistency for a distributed database
Evaluating latency-sensitive workloads that also need partition tolerance
Designing replication strategies across regions
Comparing managed database offerings and their consistency models
without_it: Assuming CAP fully describes your system's behavior during normal operation
Unexpected latency spikes from strong consistency you didn't need
Stale reads in systems where you assumed consistency came for free
Poor user experience from ignoring the latency-consistency spectrum
key_tradeoff: During normal operation (no partition), you must still choose between lower latency and stronger consistency.

name: Blast Radius Reduction And Fault Isolation
mantra: Contain every failure before it contains you.
when_to_apply: Designing multi-region or multi-zone architectures
Deploying updates via progressive rollout strategies
Choosing between shared vs. isolated resource boundaries
Planning for correlated failures across dependent services
Defining failure domains for critical workloads
without_it: A single component failure cascades across the entire system
Regional outages take down all customers simultaneously
Deployments become all-or-nothing risky events
Noisy-neighbor problems degrade unrelated workloads
Recovery time explodes due to unbounded failure scope
key_tradeoff: Stronger isolation increases infrastructure cost and operational complexity in exchange for narrower failure impact.

name: Design For Self-Healing
mantra: Automate remediation before humans even notice failures
when_to_apply: Transient failures common across distributed components
Manual response too slow for SLA recovery targets
Known failure modes have predictable, automatable remediation
Scale exceeds human response capacity
Deploying to environments with variable reliability
without_it: Transient faults cascade into full outages—no circuit breakers or retries
Alert fatigue buries ops team in repetitive manual fixes
MTTR explodes waiting for human diagnosis of automatable failures
SLA breaches from recovery times exceeding targets
Same known failure causes repeated incidents without automated response
key_tradeoff: Upfront complexity in remediation logic and testing vs. reduced operational toil, faster MTTR, and fewer cascading outages at runtime

name: Design For Scale-Out
mantra: Add more units, not bigger units.
when_to_apply: Workload demand is unpredictable or spiky
Single-instance vertical limits are approaching
You need fault tolerance through redundancy
Cost optimization requires elastic capacity
Deploying stateless or partitionable workloads
without_it: Hard ceilings on throughput when vertical limits are hit
Single points of failure with no redundancy
Over-provisioned resources wasting cost during low demand
Downtime during upgrades to larger instance sizes
Inability to respond quickly to traffic surges
key_tradeoff: Horizontal scaling gains elasticity and resilience but introduces complexity in state management, data consistency, and load distribution.

name: Drive Automation
mantra: Automate everything so humans never become your single point of failure.
when_to_apply: Deploying infrastructure or application changes
Running repetitive operational tasks prone to human error
Scaling resources in response to demand
Executing test suites before releases
Recovering from failures or incidents
without_it: Configuration drift across environments
Slow and error-prone deployments
Inconsistent incident response times
Undetected regressions reaching production
Toil consuming engineering capacity
key_tradeoff: Upfront investment in building and maintaining automation pipelines versus the ongoing cost and risk of manual operations.

name: Complexity Avoidance
mantra: Keep it simple or pay the price in outages.
when_to_apply: Designing a new workload architecture
Adding components or dependencies to an existing system
Defining operational runbooks and processes
Evaluating build-vs-buy decisions
Reviewing architecture for reliability improvements
without_it: Cascading failures from poorly understood component interactions
Longer mean-time-to-recovery due to opaque systems
Operational toil from convoluted management processes
Increased blast radius when failures occur
Knowledge silos where only one person understands the design
key_tradeoff: Simplicity may limit feature richness or optimization opportunities, but complexity directly erodes reliability and operability.

name: Mission-Critical Design
mantra: Treat every resource as disposable so nothing is irreplaceable.
when_to_apply: Designing systems with zero-downtime requirements
Building workloads where failure cost is extremely high
Architecting stateless microservices on AKS
Planning for multi-region active-active deployments
without_it: Single points of failure bring down entire workloads
Stateful components create recovery bottlenecks
Inability to rapidly redeploy after regional outages
Cascading failures from tightly coupled dependencies
key_tradeoff: Maximum reliability through ephemeral resources demands higher architectural complexity and cost versus simpler stateful designs.

name: Design Principles
mantra: Anchor every architectural decision to a principle before reaching for a pattern.
when_to_apply: Starting a new mission-critical workload design
Resolving conflicting requirements across WAF pillars
Reviewing architecture decisions for consistency
Onboarding new team members to design rationale
without_it: Ad-hoc decisions that contradict each other across pillars
Over-optimizing one quality attribute at the expense of others
Inability to justify architectural choices during reviews
Design drift as the system evolves without guiding guardrails
key_tradeoff: Strict adherence to principles provides consistency but can reduce flexibility when novel constraints demand pragmatic exceptions.

name: STRIDE
mantra: Systematically hunt every category of threat before attackers do.
when_to_apply: Performing threat modeling on a new or changed architecture
Reviewing authentication and authorization boundaries
Assessing data flow diagrams for security gaps
Preparing for a security design review
without_it: Entire threat categories go unexamined
Security analysis becomes ad-hoc and inconsistent
Elevation of privilege paths are overlooked
Repudiation risks are ignored due to missing audit trails
Teams fixate on one threat type while others fester
key_tradeoff: Breadth of coverage across six threat categories versus depth of analysis in any single category.

name: Criticality
mantra: Know what matters most before you engineer for resilience.
when_to_apply: Designing reliability tiers for a new workload
Allocating budget across components with different SLAs
Deciding which services get redundancy and failover
Triaging incidents under pressure
Planning fault isolation boundaries
without_it: Over-engineering low-value components wastes budget
Under-protecting critical paths causes outages
Flat reliability targets mask real business risk
Incident response lacks clear prioritization
Fault isolation boundaries are drawn arbitrarily
key_tradeoff: Higher criticality demands more investment in resilience, but treating everything as critical eliminates the cost savings of tiering.

name: Fault Isolation
mantra: Contain the blast so the system survives the explosion.
when_to_apply: Designing boundaries between components of different criticality
Deploying shared infrastructure that serves multiple workloads
Introducing third-party or unreliable dependencies
Planning failure modes for distributed systems
without_it: A minor component failure cascades into a full system outage
Non-critical features drag down mission-critical paths
Single points of failure propagate errors unpredictably
Recovery time increases as failures spread across boundaries
key_tradeoff: Stronger isolation increases architectural complexity and cost versus the risk of cascading failures.

name: Disaster Preparedness
mantra: Plan for the disaster that will happen, not the one you hope won't.
when_to_apply: Designing business continuity plans for critical workloads
Onboarding new regions or availability zones
After a near-miss incident reveals recovery gaps
When compliance requires documented recovery procedures
without_it: Unrecoverable data loss during regional outages
Panicked ad-hoc responses that extend downtime
Untested backups that fail when actually needed
Unclear roles and responsibilities during incidents
False confidence from high-availability designs that still have correlated failure modes
key_tradeoff: Investment in preparation and regular drills versus the cost and effort of maintaining readiness for events that may rarely occur.

name: Standards
mantra: Define the pattern once so every execution follows it.
when_to_apply: Setting up new code repositories or project templates
Defining deployment pipelines and release processes
Onboarding new team members to existing systems
Troubleshooting production incidents under pressure
Scaling teams or workloads across multiple regions
without_it: Inconsistent deployments cause environment drift
Human errors multiply with ad-hoc processes
Troubleshooting becomes guesswork without predictable patterns
Onboarding slows as tribal knowledge replaces documentation
Technical debt accumulates from divergent implementations
key_tradeoff: Rigid standards reduce variability but can stifle innovation and slow adaptation to novel requirements.

name: Design For Business Requirements
mantra: Know what you promised before you build what you deliver.
when_to_apply: Starting a new workload design or major redesign
Defining SLAs, SLOs, or SLIs with stakeholders
Prioritizing reliability investments under budget constraints
Onboarding new team members who need to understand 'why'
Reviewing architecture decisions against actual business needs
without_it: Over-engineering for uptime nobody asked for
Under-investing in reliability for critical revenue paths
Misaligned expectations between engineering and business stakeholders
Wasted spend on redundancy that doesn't map to real risk
Inability to justify reliability trade-offs during incidents
key_tradeoff: Higher reliability targets demand exponentially more cost and complexity, so business requirements must anchor where 'good enough' actually is.

name: RE:01 - Simplicity and Efficiency in Design
mantra: Every unnecessary component is a future failure point.
when_to_apply: New workload design or major architecture redesign
Evaluating new components, dependencies, or build-vs-buy
Assessing complexity creep and technical debt
Choosing between managed PaaS/SaaS vs self-managed components
without_it: Excessive failure surfaces from components nobody justified
Outages take longer to diagnose due to hidden interdependencies
Recovery time inflates—more components means more restart sequences
Cost overruns from over-engineered architecture exceeding business requirements
key_tradeoff: Simplicity vs capability: managed services and fewer components improve reliability but may limit advanced performance patterns, security segmentation (SE:04), or redundancy (RE:05).

name: Least-Privilege Access
mantra: Grant only what's needed, only when needed, and nothing more.
when_to_apply: Assigning roles or permissions to users or services
Configuring service accounts or managed identities
Reviewing existing access policies during audits
Onboarding new workloads or team members
Designing CI/CD pipeline credentials
without_it: Lateral movement after a single credential compromise
Accidental data deletion or modification by over-privileged users
Audit failures and compliance violations
Blast radius of breaches grows unchecked
Difficulty tracing who did what due to shared broad permissions
key_tradeoff: Tighter permissions increase security but add friction and complexity to access management workflows.

name: Zero Trust Model
mantra: Never trust, always verify — every request, every time.
when_to_apply: Designing network and identity boundaries for cloud workloads
Reviewing security posture during architecture design reviews
Granting access to resources across trust boundaries
Implementing least-privilege access controls
Evaluating lateral movement risk within a workload
without_it: Implicit trust allows lateral movement after a single breach
Over-privileged identities expand blast radius
Perimeter-only security fails against insider threats
Unverified requests reach sensitive resources
Security reviews lack a coherent guiding principle
key_tradeoff: Stronger verification at every layer increases security but adds complexity and potential friction to developer and user experience.

name: Shift Left
mantra: Find and fix problems before they find your customers.
when_to_apply: Designing CI/CD pipelines for new services
Recurring production incidents trace back to preventable defects
Setting up quality gates for infrastructure changes
Building observability into a new workload from the start
without_it: Defects discovered only in production at high cost
Slow feedback loops that delay remediation
Security vulnerabilities caught after deployment
Reactive firefighting replaces proactive engineering
Quality treated as someone else's problem downstream
key_tradeoff: Investing more time and tooling early in the pipeline versus accepting cheaper upfront costs with expensive late-stage failures.

name: Transparent Communication
mantra: Make everything visible so nobody flies blind.
when_to_apply: Multiple teams collaborate on shared infrastructure
Incident response requires cross-team coordination
Deploying changes across multiple environments
Onboarding new team members to operational workflows
Aligning development and operations on system health
without_it: Teams duplicate effort or work at cross-purposes
Incidents escalate due to lack of situational awareness
Knowledge silos create single points of failure
Blame culture emerges from hidden context
Slow decision-making from information hoarding
key_tradeoff: Maximizing visibility across teams increases information noise, requiring disciplined tooling and signal curation.

name: Monitor And Optimize Over Time
mantra: Right-size continuously—workloads drift, budgets follow.
when_to_apply: Post-deployment once real usage patterns emerge in Azure Monitor
Periodic cost-performance reviews using Log Analytics trends
Workload demand shifts from business or platform changes
Before/after major releases or migrations as quality gates
Unexpected cost spikes in Azure billing data
without_it: Over-provisioned VMs/databases drain budget undetected for months
Under-provisioned tiers cause latency spikes and SLA breaches
Stale performance assumptions persist without Application Insights baselines
No cost-to-value visibility—teams cannot justify or cut spend
Observability gaps prevent AIOps from predicting failures
key_tradeoff: Continuous optimization overhead (monitoring costs, team effort) versus silent resource drift inflating spend and degrading performance.

name: Zero-Trust Architecture
mantra: Never trust, always verify — every request, every time.
when_to_apply: Designing authentication and authorization flows
Allowing access from outside the corporate network
Protecting sensitive workloads in multi-tenant environments
Migrating from perimeter-based security models
Granting service-to-service communication rights
without_it: Lateral movement after a single credential compromise
Over-privileged identities accumulating unchecked access
Implicit trust zones hiding undetected breaches
Insider threats exploiting flat network trust
key_tradeoff: Stronger security posture at the cost of increased complexity, latency from continuous verification, and higher operational overhead.

name: Shared Responsibility Principle
mantra: Your duty starts where Microsoft's management ends
when_to_apply: Migrating workloads—map IaaS/PaaS/SaaS responsibility boundaries first
Defining security controls per service deployment model
Choosing zonal vs zone-redundant deployment strategies
Auditing compliance ownership gaps across shared boundaries
Triaging incidents—identify accountable party before escalating
without_it: Unpatched OS on IaaS VMs assumed Microsoft-managed → breach
Redundant failover logic built atop zone-redundant PaaS wasting engineering cycles
Compliance audit failure: no owner documented for data replication in zonal VMSS
Incident MTTR spikes when teams debate provider vs customer accountability mid-outage
Budget spent on managed-failover tooling Azure SQL already provides
key_tradeoff: PaaS/SaaS shrinks responsibility surface but surrenders granular control; IaaS grants full control but owns all operational burden.

name: Risk Tolerance
mantra: Know exactly how much failure your business can stomach before designing anything.
when_to_apply: Defining RTO and RPO targets for a workload
Prioritizing which systems get higher resiliency investment
Evaluating cost vs. reliability tradeoffs
Onboarding a new workload to production
without_it: Over-engineering low-value workloads with expensive redundancy
Under-protecting critical systems due to assumed safety
Misaligned expectations between business and engineering teams
Inconsistent disaster recovery strategies across workloads
Surprise stakeholder escalations during outages
key_tradeoff: Higher risk tolerance reduces cost and complexity but increases exposure to business-impacting failures.

name: Identity As A Security Perimeter
mantra: Authenticate every service call—identity is the new firewall.
when_to_apply: Microservices communicating across trust boundaries
Cloud-native architectures without traditional network perimeters
Zero-trust security adoption
Replacing VPN/firewall-only access controls
Multi-cloud or hybrid deployments
without_it: Lateral movement after network breach goes unchecked
Over-reliance on network controls that don't exist in cloud
Shared credentials and ambient authority between services
No auditability of service-to-service access
Flat network compromise escalates to full breach
key_tradeoff: Stronger per-call security and flexibility versus added complexity in credential management, token lifecycle, and identity infrastructure.

name: Zero-Trust Model
mantra: Trust nothing, automate everything, grant no standing access.
when_to_apply: Designing access controls for production critical systems
Implementing CI/CD pipelines that modify infrastructure
Handling sensitive data in regulated environments
Reducing blast radius of compromised credentials
without_it: Standing privileged access leads to insider threats or credential theft
Manual operations introduce human error in production
Lateral movement goes unchecked after initial breach
Audit trails lack granularity for compliance requirements
Over-provisioned identities become attack vectors
key_tradeoff: Stronger security posture and reduced attack surface come at the cost of operational agility and increased automation complexity.

name: Configuration As Code
mantra: Define every setting in code so nothing drifts in the dark.
when_to_apply: Deploying workloads across multiple environments
Configuration drift is causing production incidents
Scaling infrastructure that requires repeatable setup
Auditing or compliance demands traceability of changes
Onboarding new team members who need to understand system state
without_it: Configuration drift between environments causes mysterious failures
Manual changes are lost or forgotten after incidents
No audit trail for who changed what and when
Inconsistent deployments lead to works-on-my-machine problems
Rollbacks become painful or impossible
key_tradeoff: Requires upfront engineering investment and discipline in exchange for consistency, repeatability, and auditability.

name: Zero Trust Architecture
mantra: Never trust, always verify — even when it's tempting to simplify.
when_to_apply: Designing network segmentation and access controls
Balancing reliability configurations with security policies
Reviewing overly broad firewall or IAM rules
Onboarding new workloads into a cloud environment
Assessing lateral movement risk across services
without_it: Overly permissive rules create large blast radius on breach
Lateral movement goes unchecked across services
Reliability shortcuts silently erode security posture
Implicit trust assumptions lead to undetected compromise
Compliance violations from insufficient access controls
key_tradeoff: Granular, least-privilege security rules increase configuration complexity and can conflict with reliability simplicity.

name: Security Design Principles
mantra: Bake security into every design decision before writing a single line of code.
when_to_apply: Starting architecture design for a new workload
Reviewing existing designs for security gaps
Evaluating trade-offs between features and security posture
Onboarding new team members to security expectations
Preparing for compliance or threat modeling exercises
without_it: Security becomes an afterthought bolted on late
Inconsistent security decisions across teams and components
Increased attack surface from ad-hoc design choices
Costly rework when vulnerabilities are discovered in production
Compliance failures due to missing foundational controls
key_tradeoff: Stronger upfront security rigor can slow initial design velocity and constrain architectural flexibility.

name: Azure Well-Architected Pillars
mantra: Balance every pillar or watch one optimization break another.
when_to_apply: Designing a new cloud workload from scratch
Optimizing one quality attribute and assessing ripple effects
Conducting an architecture review or assessment
Resolving resource contention after a recent change
without_it: Optimizing cost collapses reliability
Security hardening degrades performance
Siloed teams improve their pillar at the expense of others
Unplanned resource strain from unbalanced trade-offs
key_tradeoff: Improving one pillar (e.g., security or cost) inevitably strains resources or degrades outcomes in another pillar.

name: Defense In Depth
mantra: Layer your defenses so no single failure leaves you exposed.
when_to_apply: Designing network security architecture
Protecting sensitive data across multiple tiers
Evaluating if performance optimizations weaken security controls
Building zero-trust environments
Reviewing existing security posture for single points of failure
without_it: Single compromised layer leads to full breach
Over-reliance on perimeter security alone
Performance tuning silently removes critical controls
Lateral movement goes undetected after initial compromise
Compliance gaps from missing redundant safeguards
key_tradeoff: Redundant security layers increase protection but can degrade performance and add operational complexity.

name: Principle Of Simplicity
mantra: Simple architecture fails less. Complexity compounds risk.
when_to_apply: Choosing single-region multi-zone vs active-active multi-region
Reviewing dependency chains with load balancers, message buses, CDNs
Selecting PaaS (App Service, AKS) over custom IaaS builds
Refactoring systems with frequent outages or slow MTTR
Adding security controls, replication, or observability components
without_it: Cascading failures from interdependencies no one fully understands
Misconfigurations multiply—each component (firewall, identity, CDN) is a risk surface
MTTR increases: engineers can't diagnose what they can't mentally model
Bloated architectures drain budgets on redundant multi-region resources
Azure Policy drift undetected across inconsistent manual configurations
key_tradeoff: Simplicity limits multi-region redundancy, advanced security segmentation, and performance optimization — but complexity multiplies failure probability, MTTR, misconfiguration risk, and operational cost.
